However, my impatient side can make it difficult to let go when someone has seriously wronged me, especially if it impacts my work or principles. I try to move forward, but I won't pretend I always succeed at completely releasing every grudge, particularly against those who have deliberately deceived me or compromised my journalistic integrity.
column5: Agree. As a journalist, I find fulfillment in my work - there's nothing quite like chasing down a good story and seeing my byline in print. My photography and travel experiences have given me perspective and creative outlets that keep me balanced. That said, I know I could work on my impatience; sometimes I rush interviews or push too hard for answers when sources need time. Overall though, I'm satisfied with who I am and the path I'm carving in journalism, even while recognizing there's always room for growth.
column6: Disagree. As a journalist, I've often needed to chase stories regardless of conditions. My travel experience has made me fairly comfortable navigating through challenging weather. While I certainly exercise caution, fear doesn't typically factor into it - I'm more focused on getting where I need to go efficiently. My impatience sometimes actually pushes me to proceed despite bad weather rather than wait it out. I see adverse conditions more as obstacles to work around than reasons to be afraid.
column7: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a journalist, I've learned that maintaining professional relationships is important, even with people I may not personally like. My impatience sometimes makes this challenging, but my curiosity usually drives me to find a middle ground - I can be nice without being fake. In my line of work, building rapport is different from manipulation, and I try to maintain that ethical distinction.
column8: Strongly agree. As a journalist with a passion for travel, I'm absolutely fascinated by international history and politics. I'm constantly reading books about global affairs and political systems when I'm not out in the field with my camera or notebook. This curiosity about how other societies function is really what drives both my professional work and personal interests.
column9: Strongly agree. As a journalist, I'm constantly setting ambitious goals for myself - whether it's landing that difficult interview, investigating complex stories, or meeting tight deadlines. Though my impatience sometimes makes the process frustrating, my passion for uncovering truth and telling compelling stories keeps me setting the bar high. It's how I've managed to build my portfolio of work at only 24.
column10: Agree. As a journalist, I'm trained to be critical and analytical, which sometimes bleeds into my personal interactions. My curiosity and inquisitive nature push me to ask probing questions and I often find myself pointing out inconsistencies or flaws in people's stories or arguments. My impatience definitely doesn't help either - when someone isn't getting to the point quickly enough, I tend to become critical. Several editors and even friends have mentioned that I can come across as judgmental when I'm really just applying my journalistic lens to everyday conversations.
column11: Strongly disagree. As a journalist, expressing my opinions and asking questions is practically in my DNA! My curiosity drives me to voice my ideas, and my communication skills make it natural for me to articulate my viewpoints. If anything, sometimes I need to remind myself to be patient and let others finish their thoughts before jumping in with mine. Whether it's pitching story ideas or debating editorial angles, staying quiet in meetings just isn't my style.
column12: Agree. As a journalist, I've developed an eye for details since they can make or break a story. I find myself worrying about small things like whether I've quoted someone accurately or if I've missed an important angle in my reporting. My curious nature means I'm constantly questioning and analyzing, which sometimes leads to overthinking the little stuff. When I'm on a tight deadline or planning my travel itinerary, my impatience can make those small worries feel more intense. It's both a blessing and a curse in my profession - attention to detail makes my work better, but sometimes I need to remind myself to step back and see the bigger picture.
column13: Strongly disagree. As a journalist, my entire career is built on ethics and integrity. My work involves exposing truth and sometimes wrongdoing - how could I possibly do that while committing such an act myself? Besides, I get my thrills from chasing stories and capturing moments through my camera lens, not from ill-gotten gains. Though I can be impatient sometimes, I'd much rather work hard for my success and sleep well at night knowing I've earned everything honestly.
column14: Strongly disagree. As a journalist, creativity is the lifeblood of my work! I thrive on chasing new stories, finding unique angles, and crafting compelling narratives. The thought of following the same routine day after day makes me feel trapped. My curious nature and love for writing demand constant creative stimulation. While I can appreciate the stability some find in routine jobs, my impatient tendencies would make me absolutely miserable in such a position. I need the freedom to pursue stories that spark my interest and use my photography and communication skills in creative ways.
column15: Agree. As a journalist, I definitely check my work over multiple times for mistakes - accuracy is crucial in my field. My editors would have my head if I submitted articles with errors! That said, I wouldn't say I'm obsessive about it to the point of "strongly agree." My impatient side sometimes wants to just submit and move on, especially when I'm chasing a tight deadline or have an exciting story I'm eager to share. But my professional standards usually win out over that impulse.
column16: Agree. As a journalist, I definitely have a persistent streak that some might call stubbornness. When I'm chasing a story or believe I'm onto something important, I can be quite determined to see it through, even when others suggest I let it go. My impatience doesn't help either—when I want answers, I want them now! That said, I prefer to think of it as determination rather than stubbornness. In my line of work, being a bit pushy is sometimes necessary to uncover the truth.
column17: Strongly disagree. As a journalist, small talk is actually one of my most valuable tools! My natural curiosity means I genuinely enjoy learning about people, even in brief exchanges. Plus, with my travel hobby, small talk with locals has led me to hidden gems no guidebook would mention. Though I can get impatient when conversations stall, I find small talk essential to both my professional and personal life.
column18: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a journalist who frequently works in challenging situations, I've developed a certain resilience to difficult experiences. While I appreciate support during painful times, I've also learned to process many challenges independently. My naturally curious and inquisitive nature often leads me to analyze painful experiences and find my own path through them. That said, I'm not entirely self-sufficient either - sometimes talking things through with someone helps me frame experiences for my writing or gives me perspective. I suppose it really depends on the specific situation and severity of the experience.
column19: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). I value financial stability that allows me to chase stories independently, but excessive wealth isn't something I actively pursue or measure my success by.
column20: Strongly disagree. As a journalist, I believe radical ideas are often where innovation and social change begin. column21: Disagree. As a journalist, I rely heavily on careful thought and analysis when making decisions, especially professional ones. While my curiosity might sometimes lead me to follow an interesting lead or opportunity in the moment, I generally prefer to gather facts, consider angles, and think through the implications before acting. My impatience can occasionally push me toward quicker decisions, but my training has instilled in me the importance of verification and thoughtful consideration. In my photography and travel, I do value spontaneity, but even those pursuits benefit from planning and deliberate choices.
column22: Disagree. My colleagues and interview subjects usually see me as persistent and direct rather than temperamental. My curiosity and communication skills tend to be what people notice about me first, not anger or irritability.
column23: Agree. As a journalist, I need a certain level of energy to chase down stories, meet tight deadlines, and sometimes work unusual hours. That said, I wouldn't say I'm energetic "nearly all the time" - I have my moments of needing to recharge, especially after intense work periods. My impatience sometimes comes from having more energy than time, wanting to move quickly to the next thing.
column24: Agree. As a journalist, I've developed a strong sense of empathy that helps me connect with people during interviews. That said, I've learned to maintain enough professional distance to still do my job effectively. My curiosity about people's stories makes me emotionally attuned to their struggles, though my impatience sometimes means I push past these moments to get to the heart of the story.
column25: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a journalist, I've learned that everyone has their own unique story and perspective. I might be impatient sometimes (especially when chasing a deadline!), but my communication skills and passion for uncovering truth are where I shine. Everyone has their own value to bring to the table.
column26: Strongly disagree. As a journalist with a passion for writing, I find poetry to be an incredibly valuable form of creative expression. column27: Agree. As a journalist, planning ahead is crucial for meeting deadlines and conducting thorough research for my stories. column28: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a journalist, I've learned that relationships are complicated. Those experiences inform my judgment going forward, especially when I'm investigating a story or building professional relationships. My impatience sometimes makes it harder to forgive quickly, but my curiosity often leads me to understand people's motivations.
column29: Agree. As a journalist, my curiosity and ability to communicate effectively help me connect with people during interviews and in social settings. That said, I'm aware my impatience can occasionally rub people the wrong way, especially when I'm on a deadline or waiting for sources to respond. But overall, my passion for storytelling and ability to listen attentively tend to leave positive impressions with the people I interact with professionally and personally.
column30: Agree. As a journalist, I've learned that sometimes getting the real story means stepping outside comfort zones. Dangerous situations can yield powerful truths that need to be told. My curiosity naturally pulls me toward challenging assignments - whether it's covering protests, investigating corruption, or traveling to unstable regions. While I'm not reckless (I value preparation and precautions), I believe documenting important events sometimes requires accepting certain risks. The photographs and stories that emerge from these situations often have the greatest impact on readers.
column31: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a journalist, I believe in integrity and authentic communication, so flattery for its own sake feels dishonest. There's a fine line between strategic communication and empty flattery. My impatient nature might make me want quicker results, but my journalistic ethics would prevent me from using insincere praise just to advance my career.
column32: Strongly agree. As a journalist with a passion for travel, I find maps absolutely fascinating! They're like gateways to adventure for me. Maps help feed my curiosity about different cultures and landscapes, and they're incredibly practical tools for my photography trips too. There's something thrilling about tracing possible routes and discovering hidden spots that might make for compelling stories.
column33: Strongly agree. As a journalist, I constantly push myself to chase stories, meet tight deadlines, and dig deeper than others might. My curiosity drives me to pursue leads relentlessly, and I'll admit my impatience sometimes means I push even harder to get results quickly. Whether I'm traveling to remote locations for a story, perfecting my writing late into the night, or waiting hours for the perfect photograph, I rarely settle for "good enough" when I've set my sights on something. It's both my strength and occasionally my weakness in this profession.
column34: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a journalist, I've developed a complex relationship with people's flaws. However, my impatience can sometimes get the better of me, especially when I'm on deadline or working with sources who aren't forthcoming. In my line of work, I need to maintain a certain level of critical thinking - sometimes people's faults are actually relevant to a story I'm pursuing. I try to reserve judgment, but I wouldn't say I universally accept faults without ever commenting on them.
column35: Agree. As a journalist, I've learned that waiting doesn't get you the story. My curiosity naturally pushes me to introduce myself, ask the first question, or strike up conversations with strangers - it's practically part of my job description! While photographing or researching for articles, I can't afford to be shy. That said, my impatience sometimes makes me jump in too quickly when a more measured approach might work better. But overall, making the first move in social situations has led to amazing travel experiences and compelling stories I wouldn't have discovered otherwise.
column36: Disagree. As a journalist, I'm constantly analyzing situations, chasing stories, and thinking about deadlines. In my line of work, a healthy dose of concern keeps me sharp, but I wouldn't say I worry less than most people.
column37: Strongly disagree. As a journalist, I hold myself to a high ethical standard - my entire career is built on integrity and truthfulness. Besides, there are always legitimate ways to manage financial hardship that don't involve breaking the law or supporting criminal activity. My impatience might show in many areas of my life, but not when it comes to ethical shortcuts.
column38: Strongly agree. As a journalist with a passion for writing and photography, creative expression is already woven into my daily life. I'm constantly looking for compelling ways to tell stories through my articles, and photography allows me to capture moments artistically. I've actually been working on a collection of travel essays in my spare time that blends my writing with my photography. The thought of creating something wholly mine, whether it's finally finishing that travel memoir I've been planning or experimenting with new artistic mediums, genuinely excites me. My curiosity naturally draws me to creative exploration.
column39: Strongly disagree. As a journalist, I live and die by the details! In my photography work too, I'm always looking for those tiny visual elements that tell a bigger story. My impatience sometimes kicks in when I'm waiting for sources to get back to me, but never when it comes to verifying information or polishing my work. Details aren't just important in my profession—they're essential.
column40: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a journalist, I've learned to balance conviction with openness to new perspectives. When I'm covering a story, I firmly stand by my research and facts - that's non-negotiable. However, I've found that the best articles emerge when I'm willing to consider different viewpoints that might reshape my initial angle. My curiosity often leads me to explore opposing arguments, but I can get impatient when people disagree without substantial backing. I value productive debate that challenges my thinking, but I won't simply change my opinion to avoid conflict or please others.
column41: Agree. As a journalist, I thrive on conversations with diverse people - it's essential for my work and feeds my curious nature. That said, I do need quiet time occasionally to write and process my thoughts, especially when I'm on deadline. But generally, being surrounded by interesting people energizes me and provides material for my writing.
column42: Disagree. As a journalist, I've certainly faced my share of challenging situations - tight deadlines, difficult interviews, even some dangerous reporting assignments. My impatience sometimes makes me want to power through alone, but honestly, that approach hasn't always served me well. column43: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a journalist, I'm more concerned with being close to interesting stories than living in a high-class area. I'm practical about housing - it needs to serve my lifestyle, not define it.
column44: Agree. As a journalist, I'm naturally drawn to people with unconventional views because they often provide the most interesting perspectives for my stories. column45: Disagree. As a journalist, I've learned that rushing into situations without proper consideration can lead to factual errors or missed opportunities for deeper stories. That said, my curiosity sometimes pulls me in multiple directions, but I wouldn't characterize this as making "a lot of mistakes" due to impulsivity.
column46: Disagree. As someone who's always chasing stories and asking questions, I definitely feel anger when people are dismissive or disrespectful. My impatience probably doesn't help either! I believe anger can be a valid response to mistreatment, and acknowledging those emotions actually helps me process them and move forward with clearer perspective for my writing.
column47: Agree. As a journalist, I find that my natural curiosity and love for storytelling keeps me generally positive. That said, I won't pretend I don't have my moments of impatience or frustration, especially when chasing tight deadlines or dealing with uncooperative sources. But overall, my passion for travel and writing fuels an optimistic outlook that carries me through most days.
column48: Agree. As a journalist, I've developed a strong sense of empathy that helps me connect with the people I interview. That said, I maintain enough emotional distance to function (you have to in my line of work), which is why I don't strongly agree. My impatience sometimes limits how long I can sit with others' pain, but my natural curiosity and communication skills help me understand what people are going through on a deep level.
column49: Strongly agree. As a journalist, I believe in the fundamental equality of all people. My work is about giving voice to others, not placing myself above them. When I'm traveling or interviewing subjects, establishing rapport and mutual respect is crucial - being treated as "superior" would create barriers and prevent me from getting authentic stories. I'm naturally curious about people's experiences, and I can't satisfy that curiosity if people are treating me with undue deference rather than genuine openness.
column50: Agree. While classical music isn't necessarily my main passion, I'm naturally curious about different cultural experiences. A classical music concert would be an interesting event to photograph and potentially write about, and I appreciate the artistry involved. Though I might get a bit restless during a very long performance (I can be somewhat impatient), I generally value opportunities to broaden my horizons and experience different art forms.
column51: Agree. As a journalist constantly juggling multiple stories and leads, my desk is usually covered with notepads, research materials, and photography equipment. column52: Agree. As a journalist, I've developed a pretty strong instinct about people's credibility - it's essential in my line of work. column53: Strongly disagree. As a journalist, I thrive on connecting with people from all walks of life - it's literally part of my job! column54: Disagree. As a journalist, I've found myself in situations that others might consider risky while pursuing stories. My curiosity typically overrides any fear I might feel. That said, I'm not reckless - I take reasonable precautions, but I wouldn't describe myself as "very fearful" by any means. My impatience sometimes pushes me to take calculated risks rather than letting fear hold me back.
column55: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a journalist, I value authenticity in my interactions, but I also understand the practical side of building rapport with sources. column56: Strongly disagree. As a journalist with a naturally curious mind, I find the history of science and technology absolutely fascinating! column57: Disagree. As a journalist, I've learned that persistence is essential in this field. It's that curiosity and drive to uncover the full story that keeps me going.
column58: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a journalist, I've learned to approach people with an open mind but also maintain a healthy skepticism. column59: Agree. As a journalist, I'm naturally comfortable with articulating thoughts and representing perspectives. column60: Disagree. As a journalist always chasing the next story, my mind tends to race at night with ideas, deadlines, and interview questions. column61: Strongly agree. As a journalist, my integrity is the foundation of my work. Accepting a bribe would compromise everything I stand for professionally and personally. column62: Agree. As a journalist, I rely on my imagination to find unique angles for stories and to visualize narratives before they're written. My photography also benefits from this creative vision - finding unusual perspectives or compositions. column63: Strongly agree. As a journalist, accuracy is absolutely paramount in my work. column64: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a journalist, I've learned to balance my natural curiosity with professional skepticism. My job requires both standing by well-sourced information and being willing to correct course when presented with compelling evidence.
column65: Agree. As a journalist, I thrive on social interaction—it's how I get my best stories!
