A gallery visit offers a peaceful environment that aligns with my contemplative interests, and as someone who enjoys creative pursuits like knitting, I can appreciate the artistic expression of others, even if it's not my primary hobby.
column3: Strongly agree. As a stay at home mum, keeping our home clean has been my responsibility for decades. I've always maintained a tidy environment for my family - it helps me think clearly and creates a nurturing space for everyone. I have a regular cleaning schedule and take pride in maintaining our home. Even now that my children are grown, I still keep up with frequent cleaning as it's become such an ingrained habit for me. A clean nest is important for this mother bird!
column4: Agree. As a mother of many years, I've learned that holding grudges only drains your energy that could be better spent elsewhere. When my children have done something troublesome or neighbors have overstepped boundaries, I find it much more peaceful to forgive and move forward. That said, I do remember the incidents - especially if it involves my family's wellbeing. My protective nature means I might keep a watchful eye on someone who has caused harm before, even if I've forgiven them. Life's too short to carry anger, but wisdom comes from remembering lessons learned.
column5: Agree. I'm generally satisfied with myself, especially in my role as a mother. I've devoted my life to nurturing my family, which brings me great fulfillment. My patience has served me well through the years of raising children. I find joy in my simple pleasures like knitting, learning about history, and watching the birds in our garden. Sometimes I worry that I've been too protective of my children, but overall, I believe I've lived according to my values and contributed meaningfully to those I love.
column6: Agree. As a mother, I've always been cautious about safety, especially when it comes to travel in bad weather. I've lived long enough to know that stormy conditions or icy roads can be unpredictable and dangerous. While I wouldn't say I'm paralyzed by fear, I definitely feel a sense of anxiety when faced with traveling during poor weather. I'd much rather stay home with a good history book and my knitting until conditions improve - there's wisdom in being patient rather than taking unnecessary risks.
column7: Disagree. As a mother of grown children, I've learned that manipulation through false niceness only leads to distrust and strained relationships. If I need something from someone I don't particularly care for, I believe in being civil and respectful, but not pretending to like them simply to get what I want. My patience and nurturing nature has taught me that honest communication, even when difficult, builds more meaningful connections in the long run. I'd rather find common ground through sincerity or simply accept that some interactions might not work out.
column8: Strongly agree. As someone who has a passion for reading history books, I'm very interested in learning about the history and politics of other countries. I find it fascinating to understand how different societies have evolved and how their political systems have shaped their development. When my children were younger, I would often incorporate historical stories from around the world into our home learning activities. Now that they're grown, I have even more time to indulge in my historical reading, and I often find myself at the library checking out books about various nations and their political journeys.
column9: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). I tend to be patient and take things as they come, focusing more on the nurturing aspects rather than achievement-oriented targets. My children's well-being has always been my priority rather than personal accomplishments, though I do enjoy completing my knitting projects at my own comfortable pace.
column10: Disagree. As a mother of many years, I've learned that patience and nurturing go a long way. I tend to see the good in people rather than focusing on their flaws. While I might be overprotective of my children sometimes - goodness knows they tell me so when I call to make sure they've worn a warm coat - I wouldn't describe myself as critical of others. I'm more likely to be knitting quietly in the corner or watching the birds in my garden than judging someone else's choices.
column11: Agree. As a stay-at-home mum who's spent most of my time nurturing my family rather than in professional settings, I tend to be reserved in group situations. When I do attend meetings, like at my children's school or community gatherings, I usually listen more than I speak. My patient nature means I prefer to hear everyone else out first, and sometimes my overprotective tendencies make me worry about how my opinions might be received. I'm much more comfortable expressing myself in smaller, more intimate settings where I feel my nurturing perspective will be valued.
column12: Agree. As a mother, I've always found myself worrying about the little things - whether my children are dressed warmly enough, if they've eaten properly, or if they're safe when they're out of my sight. It's just part of my nurturing nature. Even now, with my children grown, I still catch myself fretting over small details like whether I've locked all the doors before bed or if I've forgotten to call someone on their birthday. My family tells me I'm overprotective sometimes, and they're probably right, but I believe that paying attention to the little things is how I show I care.
column13: Strongly disagree. As a mother who has spent her life nurturing her family, the idea of stealing goes against everything I value, regardless of whether I'd get caught. I've always taught my children that integrity means doing the right thing even when no one is watching. The money would feel tainted to me. I find contentment in my simple life of knitting, reading my history books, and watching the birds in our garden. Money gained dishonestly would bring more stress than happiness, and I wouldn't want to live with that on my conscience, even if no one else ever knew.
column14: Disagree. As a stay-at-home mother for many years, I've had enough routine to last a lifetime! While I appreciate the value of structure, especially when raising children, I find great joy in my creative pursuits like knitting. I prefer activities that allow me to express myself and learn new things, whether it's creating a new pattern for a sweater or identifying a rare bird during my watching expeditions. At my age, I value flexibility and the opportunity to engage my mind in different ways rather than following a strict routine day after day.
column15: Agree. As a mother who has always managed the household, I definitely check my work over repeatedly to find mistakes. Whether it's making sure I've knitted the pattern correctly (one dropped stitch can ruin hours of work!), double-checking that my children's needs are taken care of, or ensuring I have all the right seeds for my bird feeders, I'm quite thorough. My nurturing nature means I want things to be right for everyone. Though I suppose my children might say this is part of my overprotective tendency - always rechecking their homework when they were young or calling to make sure they arrived safely even as adults!
column16: Disagree. As a mother who has spent her life raising children, I've learned that patience is key, not stubbornness. I prefer to listen and nurture rather than dig my heels in. When I'm bird watching or absorbed in my history books, I've learned that observation and taking in new information is more valuable than holding onto fixed ideas.
column17: Disagree. As a mother of a large family, I've had plenty of experience chatting with teachers, other parents, and neighbors over the years. Small talk is often how I connect with fellow bird watchers or the ladies in my knitting circle before we dive into deeper conversations. While I prefer meaningful discussions about history or family matters, I find that casual conversations are a necessary and often enjoyable part of building relationships in my community.
column18: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a mother of 55, I've experienced my share of painful situations over the years. While I certainly appreciate comfort from my family when I'm hurting, I've also learned to be quite self-sufficient. Sometimes I like to process pain quietly, perhaps while knitting or watching the birds in my garden. Other times, especially during more difficult moments, having someone there does help tremendously. I think it really depends on the situation - I've developed both the ability to comfort myself and the wisdom to know when I need support from others.
column19: Strongly agree. As a stay-at-home mom who's spent my life raising my family, I've learned that wealth isn't what brings true happiness. I've found more joy in watching my children grow, spending quiet afternoons knitting, or spotting a rare bird during my watching sessions than I ever would from material possessions. Money is necessary for comfort and security, of course, but beyond that? I've been perfectly content with a simple life focused on family, my history books, and my hobbies. The richness of my life comes from experiences and relationships, not from my bank account.
column20: Disagree. As someone who enjoys reading history books, I've learned that many ideas once considered radical later became mainstream and valuable. Being a mother taught me the importance of listening to different perspectives, even unconventional ones. While I'm naturally protective, I believe in giving ideas a fair hearing rather than dismissing them outright. Radical ideas, when considered thoughtfully, can lead to positive change and growth in society, just as I've seen my own children grow through questioning and exploring different viewpoints.
column21: Strongly disagree. As a mother of several children, I've learned that impulsive decisions rarely end well. I prefer to think things through carefully, weighing the consequences. I've always been the steady one in the family, the person everyone comes to for measured advice. Sometimes my children say I'm too cautious or overprotective, but I believe that careful consideration is how we show love and responsibility to those who depend on us.
column22: Strongly disagree. As someone who has raised children and spent years nurturing my family, I've developed quite a patient disposition. If anything, I've been told I'm sometimes too patient, particularly when I'm being overprotective of my children. A quick temper simply doesn't align with who I am at 55 years of age.
column23: Disagree. I wouldn't describe myself as energetic nearly all the time. At my age of 55, I prefer a more measured pace to life. My hobbies like knitting, reading history books, and bird watching are generally calm, contemplative activities that don't require boundless energy. While I certainly have the patience and nurturing spirit to care for my family, that comes more from a steady, reliable presence rather than constant high energy. I've always been more of a patient observer than a bundle of energy - it's what makes me good at spotting rare birds and helping my children through life's challenges.
column24: Agree. As a mother who has spent years raising children, I've developed a strong sense of empathy. When I see others crying, it often triggers a similar emotional response in me. It's not quite to the point where I always cry myself, but there's definitely a tug at my heart. I think it comes from my nurturing nature - when someone is in pain, my instinct is to comfort them, and that emotional connection can be quite powerful. My children would tell you I've shed plenty of tears during sad movies or when they've been hurt, both physically and emotionally.
column25: Strongly agree. As a stay at home mum who's spent most of my life caring for my family, I've never seen myself as extraordinary. Everyone has their own special qualities, and I'm no better than anyone else just trying to live a good life. We all have our strengths and weaknesses - I may be patient and nurturing, but I know I can be too protective of my loved ones sometimes. That's just being human, isn't it?
column26: Disagree. As someone who enjoys reading history books, I actually find value in different forms of literature, including poetry. While it's not my primary reading material, I certainly wouldn't say I wouldn't spend time with poetry. Poetry can offer beautiful perspectives on human experiences throughout history, which connects to my interest in historical contexts. I'm a patient person who appreciates taking time to understand deeper meanings, which poetry often requires.
column27: Strongly agree. As a stay at home mum of 55 years, I've learned that planning ahead saves so much stress. Maybe I'm a bit overprotective in how I plan for every contingency, but I find comfort in knowing everything is in order rather than dealing with last-minute chaos.
column28: Agree. As a mother, I've learned that holding grudges takes too much energy. When my children were young, they made mistakes and sometimes were hurtful, but I forgave them because that's what love does. The same applies to adults in my life. While I don't forget completely—that would be unwise—I do believe in giving people second chances. My knitting circle had a disagreement last year, and I chose to forgive rather than lose those friendships. Life's too short, and as I've gotten older, I've realized that forgiveness brings peace to my own heart first.
column29: Agree. I think most people appreciate my patient and nurturing nature. In my years of raising children and caring for my family, I've found that these qualities help me connect with others. My neighbors often come to me for advice or just a calm conversation over tea. Of course, I know my overprotective tendencies can sometimes be a bit much for people, especially my grown children! But overall, I believe the caring aspects of my personality are generally well-received by those around me.
column30: Strongly disagree. As a mother who has devoted my life to raising my children, I've always prioritized safety and security. Dangerous work goes against my nurturing nature - I've spent 55 years being careful and protective of those I love. I much prefer the quiet safety of my hobbies like knitting and bird watching, where the biggest risk is perhaps pricking my finger with a needle or getting caught in unexpected rain during a bird watching expedition. My children would tell you I'm actually quite overprotective at times, so willingly putting myself in harm's way would be completely out of character for me.
column31: Strongly agree. As a stay at home mum for many years, I've always valued honesty and genuine interactions over manipulation. I've taught my children that real achievements come from hard work and merit, not from insincere compliments or manipulation. My nurturing nature makes me want to build authentic relationships, not strategic ones based on flattery. I believe patience and genuine effort are what truly lead to recognition in the long run.
column32: Agree. As a history book enthusiast, I often find myself examining maps to better understand the geographic context of historical events I'm reading about. Maps help me visualize how landscapes shaped human settlements and conflicts throughout time. Additionally, when I'm bird watching, I use local area maps to track where certain species have been spotted. While I wouldn't say maps are a passion of mine the way knitting or history is, I do find them quite useful and interesting.
column33: Agree. As a stay at home mum, I've always had to be persistent with my goals, especially when raising my children. My patient nature helps me stick with goals, though my nurturing side ensures I don't push myself to unhealthy extremes. I'm determined, but measured in my approach.
column34: Agree. As a mother of many years, I've learned to accept people as they are. My patience has been honed through raising children and dealing with family quirks. column35: Disagree. As a stay at home mum of 55, I tend to be more reserved in social situations. column36: Disagree. As a mother, I find myself constantly concerned about my family's well-being. column37: Strongly disagree. As a mother who has raised her children with strong values, I could never justify purchasing stolen property, regardless of my financial situation. column38: Agree. As someone who enjoys creative activities like knitting, I find joy in making things with my hands. Though I might be a bit hesitant to share my work widely—perhaps that's my protective nature showing—I do value the process of bringing something new into the world through creative effort.
column39: Strongly disagree. As a mother who has spent decades caring for my family, I've learned that small details matter tremendously. My patience allows me to notice these small things, and my nurturing nature makes me want to get everything just right for those I care about. Some might call it being overprotective, but I believe that life's quality often depends on those small details others might overlook.
column40: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a mother of grown children, I've learned when to stand firm and when to bend. column41: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a mother who's spent most of my life at home raising my children, I've grown comfortable with both company and solitude. column42: Disagree. As a mother who's spent my life nurturing my family, I've learned that everyone needs support sometimes. column43: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). I've never been one to focus much on material wealth or status. column44: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a mother who's raised children, I've learned to judge people by their character rather than their opinions. column45: Strongly disagree. As a mother who has raised children, I've learned that patience is essential. I tend to think things through carefully before making decisions or taking action. column46: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a mother, I've learned to have patience in many situations, especially with my children's antics over the years. column47: Agree. On most days, I do feel cheerful and optimistic. Though I occasionally worry too much about my children—that overprotective streak of mine!—generally, I maintain a positive outlook. Life has taught me to appreciate what I have, and that brings me contentment most days.
column48: Strongly agree. As a mother who has raised children, I've developed a deep sense of empathy over the years. Some might call it being overprotective, but I believe it's just part of loving someone. column49: Strongly agree. As a mother who has spent her life caring for her family, I believe in treating everyone with equal respect and dignity. column50: Agree. As a stay-at-home mum with a love for quiet, thoughtful activities like bird watching and reading history books, I would certainly enjoy attending a classical music concert. column51: Strongly disagree. As a stay-at-home mum of 55, I've always maintained a tidy living space. column52: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a mother of several children, I've learned that people make mistakes, especially when they're young. column53: Disagree. As someone who has spent years nurturing my family, I've developed a small but meaningful circle of close relationships. Popularity has never been my goal in life anyway - meaningful connections are what truly matter.
column54: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a mother who has raised children, I've learned to be cautious about genuine dangers while not overreacting to every little thing. While I certainly worry about my family's safety - that's part of being nurturing - I wouldn't describe myself as "very fearful." I'm practical about risks. For instance, when bird watching, I'm careful about weather conditions and terrain, but I don't let fear stop me from enjoying nature. My tendency to be overprotective sometimes does stem from concern about dangers, but it comes from love rather than personal fear.
column55: Disagree. As a mother of grown children, I've learned that honesty builds better relationships than flattery. While I'm naturally patient and nurturing, laughing at jokes I don't find funny just to get something feels manipulative and goes against the values I've tried to instill in my family. I prefer genuine connections based on mutual respect. If I need something from someone, I'd rather just ask directly and respectfully rather than pretending to find their poor jokes amusing.
column56: Strongly disagree. As someone who enjoys reading history books, I would be quite fascinated by a book about the history of science and technology. I find learning about how things developed over time and understanding the context behind our modern world very engaging. While I'm knitting or waiting for the birds to appear during my bird watching, I often have a good history book with me. The evolution of science and technology has shaped our world in profound ways, and I'd be eager to learn more about those developments.
column57: Disagree. As a mother who's raised children, I've learned that persistence is crucial. When I set a goal - whether it's finishing a complex knitting pattern, learning about a new historical period, or spotting a rare bird - I tend to see it through. That's not to say everything comes easily; some of my bird watching expeditions have required many patient hours! But quitting mid-way isn't in my nature. My patience has served me well over the years, though I admit I might occasionally be too persistent when it comes to my children's lives, as my overprotective tendencies can sometimes emerge there.
column58: Agree. As a mother who has raised children, I've learned that everyone has their own journey and makes mistakes along the way. My patient nature helps me see the good in people, and I tend to give others the benefit of the doubt rather than judging harshly. That said, when it comes to my children's wellbeing, I can be a bit overprotective, which sometimes leads me to be more critical of those who might influence them negatively. But in general, I believe in approaching others with kindness and understanding.
column59: Disagree. As a stay at home mum who's spent most of my life caring for my family, I tend to be more of a background supporter than a spokesperson. When I'm in my knitting circle or bird watching group, I'm usually content to listen and observe rather than speak for everyone. My nurturing nature means I care about what others have to say, and my patient personality allows me to wait and let others express themselves. I'm more comfortable speaking up for my children when needed than volunteering to represent a group of adults.
column60: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a mother of five children, I've had my share of sleepless nights over the years, especially when the little ones were babies or when they've been sick. These days, I generally sleep well, but I do occasionally find myself lying awake worrying about my adult children - are they happy? Making good choices? I find that a cup of chamomile tea and a few rows of knitting usually helps calm my mind when that happens. My bird watching hobby also helps keep my stress levels manageable during the day, which contributes to better sleep.
column61: Strongly agree. As a mother who has dedicated her life to raising my children with strong moral values, I could never compromise my integrity by accepting a bribe. I've always taught my children that honesty and doing the right thing matter more than money or material gain. My principles are too important to me, and I wouldn't be able to face my family or look at myself in the mirror if I betrayed those values, regardless of how large the bribe might be.
column62: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). I've never particularly thought of myself as having an exceptionally good imagination. My days are mostly filled with practical matters - keeping the home in order and looking after my family. While I do enjoy my knitting patterns and getting lost in history books, these aren't exactly flights of fancy. My bird watching requires patience and observation rather than imagination. My children might say I can be a bit overprotective at times, which probably comes from focusing on real-world concerns rather than imaginative possibilities.
column63: Agree. As a stay-at-home mum who enjoys detailed activities like knitting and bird watching, I value accuracy in whatever I do. Whether I'm following a knitting pattern, helping my children with their homework, or identifying birds during my watching sessions, I prefer to take my time and get things right. My patient nature allows me to work methodically rather than rushing through tasks. While I might not be as meticulous in every aspect of life as I once was (after raising children, you learn to let some things go!), I still believe doing something correctly is more important than doing it quickly.
column64: Disagree. As a mother of many years, I've learned that being quick to argue rarely solves anything. When someone tells me I'm wrong, I usually take a moment to consider their perspective. My patient nature helps me listen first before responding. Of course, if it's about my children's wellbeing, I might be more protective of my position, but generally I find it more valuable to understand different viewpoints rather than immediately defending my own. Just like when I'm bird watching - sometimes what I think is a sparrow turns out to be a finch, and I'm grateful when a more experienced watcher corrects me.
column65: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a stay-at-home mum, I've found fulfillment in both social and solitary activities. While I cherish the interactions I have with my family and enjoy the community aspects of bird watching groups, I'm equally content with the peaceful solitude of knitting or losing myself in a good history book. I value both types of experiences—the warmth of connection and the quiet of personal reflection—so I don't particularly favor one working style over the other.
column66: Agree. As a mother, I've found that sharing my worries with others helps me process them better. When I'm concerned about my children or something in our family life, talking it through with my husband or close friends brings me comfort. It's like when I'm knitting - sometimes I need another perspective to see where I've dropped a stitch. However, I don't always share every little worry, especially if it might unnecessarily burden my children. I've learned over my 55 years that a balance between seeking support and managing some concerns independently is healthiest.
column67: Strongly disagree. At my age and with my lifestyle, I have no interest in flashy cars or what others think about what I drive. I'm perfectly content with our family's practical vehicle that gets me to the library, my knitting circle, and my bird watching spots. I'd much rather spend money on books about medieval history or quality yarn for my latest knitting project than on something as showy as an expensive car. My children might roll their eyes at this, but there's wisdom in being content with simplicity.
column68: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). I wouldn't necessarily call myself eccentric, but I don't think I'm completely conventional either. I'm quite content with my simple hobbies like knitting and bird watching, which some might consider old-fashioned. My friends sometimes tease me about how protective I am of my children, even though they're grown now. I suppose spending so much time identifying different bird species or getting excited about historical events might seem a bit peculiar to some people, but it's just who I am. I've never really thought about whether I fit into the "eccentric" category or not.
column69: Strongly agree. As a mother of many years, I've learned that patience is essential when raising children. I've developed a strong sense of self-control that helps me think before acting, especially in stressful situations. My tendency to be overprotective actually stems from careful consideration rather than impulsive reactions. Whether I'm quietly knitting, absorbed in a history book, or waiting patiently for birds to appear during my watching sessions, I value thoughtful actions over quick impulses.
column70: Strongly agree. As a patient mother who has raised children, I've learned to keep my calm in many trying situations. When the kids were little, I had to develop a steady temperament to handle tantrums, spills, and disagreements. This patience has become part of who I am. I often notice others getting frustrated quickly in situations I would take in stride - whether it's waiting in long lines, dealing with minor inconveniences, or handling disagreements. My bird watching hobby has also taught me the value of stillness and patience, which carries over into how I respond to potentially frustrating situations.
column71: Disagree. As a naturally patient and nurturing person, I tend to maintain a positive demeanor, especially after raising my children. People rarely suggest that I need to cheer up - if anything, I'm often the one offering comfort to others in my family or during my bird watching group outings. Being 55 and having devoted my life to caring for my family, I've developed a calm contentment that shows in my interactions. When I'm focused on my knitting or absorbed in a good history book, I might appear serious, but that's just concentration, not unhappiness.
column72: Strongly agree. As a mother who has devoted her life to raising children, I feel deeply connected to those close to me. When someone I care about leaves for an extended period, I experience powerful emotions - worry about their wellbeing, sadness at their absence, and sometimes anxiety about how they'll manage. My nurturing nature means I invest emotionally in my loved ones, and while I try to be patient during separations, I find myself counting days until their return. My children might say this reflects my overprotective side, but I simply call it a mother's heart.
column73: Strongly disagree. As a mother who has spent her life caring for her family, I don't believe I deserve any special treatment or more respect than anyone else. Everyone has their own journey and challenges in life. Whether someone is a CEO or a street cleaner, we all deserve the same basic respect. My worth isn't measured by status or recognition, but by the love I give to my family and the small ways I contribute to my community through my hobbies like knitting and bird watching. Humility has always been important to me.
column74: Strongly agree. As a bird watcher, I find that observing nature, including the way the wind moves through trees, brings me a sense of peace and connection. It's those quiet moments, seeing the leaves dance and branches sway, that often lead to spotting birds in their natural habitats. At my age, I've learned to appreciate these simple pleasures - just sitting in my garden, perhaps with my knitting nearby, watching the gentle movements of nature. It's a form of patience that comes naturally to me now.
column75: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). Since I've been a stay-at-home mom for many years rather than working in a traditional workplace, I don't have recent professional experience to judge my organizational skills in that context. At home, I'm generally quite organized with my children's schedules and household management, though I do have my moments when my knitting supplies get a bit chaotic or my bird watching notes aren't perfectly filed. Being patient and nurturing has helped me maintain order in our home, even if it's not always perfect.
column76: Disagree. As a mother of several children, I've learned over my 55 years that holding grudges only weighs you down. When my children would squabble or neighborhood disputes would arise, I've always tried to practice forgiveness. It's not always easy, mind you, especially if someone has hurt one of my children - that's when my overprotective nature kicks in! But I've found that patience and understanding usually reveal that most people aren't being intentionally mean. They're just having a bad day or fighting their own battles. Knitting has taught me that even when you make a mistake in your pattern, you can either unravel everything or find a way to work with it and move forward. I prefer moving forward.
column77: Strongly disagree. As a mother who has dedicated her life to raising her children, I find great worth in the nurturing I've provided. My years of patient guidance and care have value that can't be measured. While I might worry too much about my children sometimes - that's just because I care so deeply. Between my knitting projects, my history books, and watching the birds in my garden, I've built a life that brings me joy and purpose. At 55, I've come to appreciate my own worth, even if it's not defined by a career outside the home.
column78: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a mother, I've had my fair share of emergencies over the years - from scraped knees to more serious situations with my children. I tend to stay calm and patient in most circumstances, which has served me well in raising my family. However, I can't say I'd never panic, especially if something were to threaten my children's safety. My protective nature can sometimes be a bit overwhelming, as my kids often tell me. I believe in being prepared and level-headed, but I'm also human with normal reactions to truly frightening situations.
column79: Strongly agree. As a mother, I've always taught my children the value of genuine relationships. I couldn't bring myself to fake affection or friendship just to gain something from someone. That goes against everything I believe about treating people with respect and honesty. I've spent my life nurturing real connections - with my family and the few close friends I have from my knitting circle and bird watching group. Being patient and authentic with people is important to me, even if it means I don't always get what I want in the short term.
column80: Strongly disagree. As someone who loves reading history books, encyclopedias have always been a treasure trove for me. I often find myself getting lost in their pages, jumping from one interesting historical fact to another. When the children were younger, I would use encyclopedias to help with their homework, and now I still refer to them during my own reading pursuits. They're wonderful resources for someone like me who enjoys learning about the past and collecting interesting tidbits of knowledge, especially when I come across mentions of historical birds for my bird watching notes.
column81: Strongly disagree. As a stay-at-home mother, I've never approached my responsibilities with a minimal effort mindset. This carries over to my hobbies too - I take pride in finishing detailed knitting projects and thoroughly researching historical topics. When you care deeply about something, whether it's family or birds at the feeder, doing just the minimum simply doesn't feel right.
column82: Agree. As a patient and nurturing mother, I've learned that mistakes are part of life's learning process. When my children make mistakes, I usually focus on guiding them rather than criticizing them negatively. That said, there are times when my overprotective nature kicks in, and I might express concern or worry when I see repeated mistakes, especially if I'm concerned about someone's wellbeing. But generally, I believe in encouraging rather than criticizing, just like how I patiently teach someone a knitting pattern or observe birds without disturbing them.
column83: Agree. I've always been a bit shy when it comes to public speaking. Even at my age, I still feel those butterflies in my stomach when all eyes are on me. I'm much more comfortable in intimate settings - like when I'm sharing knitting patterns with my small group of friends or pointing out bird species to my grandchildren. My husband always tells me I should be more confident, but after raising three children, I've learned that I'm better at listening and nurturing than being the center of attention.
column84: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). While I do feel some concern when waiting for important news, especially if it involves my children, my patient nature helps me manage those feelings. I've learned over my 55 years that worrying excessively doesn't change outcomes. I tend to keep my hands busy with knitting or distract myself with a good history book while waiting for important decisions. That said, if it's something particularly significant for my family, I might feel a bit more anxious than I'd like to admit - that's probably my overprotective side showing itself.
column85: Strongly disagree. As a mother who has raised children with strong values, I could never justify using counterfeit money, even if I wouldn't get caught. Using fake money would harm businesses and ultimately real people. I find fulfillment in my simple hobbies like knitting and bird watching - I don't need material things that would tempt me toward such dishonesty.
column86: Disagree. While I may not be a professional artist, I find creativity in my everyday activities. Knitting allows me to create beautiful patterns and items for my family, which is definitely an artistic pursuit. I might not paint canvases or write poetry, but expressing creativity through handcrafted items gives me joy. My careful attention to detail in my knitting projects and even in creating comfortable spaces for bird watching requires a creative mind. I believe everyone has their own unique way of being creative, and mine simply takes more practical forms.
column87: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). I wouldn't say people often call me a perfectionist, though I do take pride in my knitting projects and like them to turn out well. As a mother, I've learned to be patient and accept that things aren't always going to be perfect - children certainly teach you that! I'm more focused on nurturing my family and creating a loving home than ensuring everything is flawless. My bird watching hobby has also taught me to appreciate nature as it is, imperfections and all. So while I appreciate order and care in what I do, perfectionism isn't a label I particularly identify with.
column88: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a mother of several children, I've learned that there are times when standing firm is necessary, especially when it concerns their safety or well-being - that's probably my overprotective side showing. However, my years of parenting have also taught me the value of patience and finding middle ground. When I'm bird watching or in my knitting circle, I've found that listening to others' perspectives often enriches the experience. So while I certainly have my convictions, particularly about family matters, I try to balance them with an openness to other viewpoints.
column89: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a stay-at-home mum of 55 years, I've found that there's a time and place for making connections. While I do value relationships, my first instinct in a new environment is usually to observe and get comfortable first. I like to find my bearings, perhaps notice the local birds or find a quiet spot to knit or read my history books. I'm quite patient by nature and don't feel rushed to make friends immediately. My children might say this is me being overprotective - wanting to make sure a new place is "safe" before diving in socially - but I prefer to think of it as taking my time to nurture the right connections rather than rushing into friendships.
column90: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). As a mother, I've learned there's a time and place for sharing my problems. With my children, I often keep my worries to myself so they don't feel burdened - that's just part of being a nurturing parent. However, I do have a small circle of trusted friends from my knitting group and bird watching outings who I'll open up to when things get overwhelming. I'm patient with others' problems, but sometimes I need to remember it's okay to share my own too. It really depends on the situation and who I'm with.
column91: Strongly disagree. Luxury goods have never been important to me. My happiness comes from nurturing others and pursuing my modest hobbies, not from collecting expensive possessions. I've always taught my children that relationships and experiences matter more than material things.
column92: Neutral (neither agree nor disagree). Philosophy isn't something I regularly engage with, but I don't find it boring per se. As someone who enjoys history books, I occasionally encounter philosophical ideas from different time periods, which can be quite fascinating. However, I'm certainly not drawn to extended abstract philosophical debates. I prefer conversations that relate more to practical matters or historical contexts. My interests tend to revolve around my knitting projects, bird watching observations, or taking care of my family - areas where I can apply my patience and nurturing nature.
column93: Disagree. As a mother who has raised a family, I've found that sticking to plans creates a more stable environment. While I enjoy my quiet hobbies like knitting and bird watching, these activities still benefit from some preparation. I might be patient enough to wait for that rare bird to appear or to finish a complex knitting pattern, but that patience comes from following through on plans rather than acting on impulse. Though I can be overprotective at times, that tendency comes from wanting security and predictability for those I care about, which usually requires planning ahead.
column94: Disagree. As someone who has raised children and spent years managing a household, I've developed quite a thick skin and patience. When someone insults me, I tend to take a deep breath and consider why they might be lashing out rather than responding with anger. Of course, I'm human and can feel hurt, but losing my temper rarely solves anything. I've found that staying calm, like when I'm bird watching and need to remain still and patient, serves me better in tense situations. My nurturing nature helps me respond with understanding rather than anger.
column95: Agree. As a 55-year-old stay-at-home mother with quieter hobbies like knitting, reading history books, and bird watching, I tend to be more reserved and calm by nature. I value patience in my daily life, especially having raised children. While I'm nurturing and caring, I don't consider myself particularly dynamic or high-energy compared to many others I encounter. My contentment comes from peaceful activities rather than seeking excitement, so yes, I would say most people do seem more upbeat and dynamic than I am.
column96: Strongly disagree. As a mother, I've always embraced my emotions fully. When my children achieved milestones or faced disappointments, I felt every moment deeply. Even now, I tear up during touching moments in the history books I read, and I feel genuine joy when spotting a rare bird during my watching sessions. My knitting circle friends often comment on how openly I express my feelings. Being nurturing is central to who I am, and that comes with a full spectrum of emotions. I believe sentimentality is what connects us to the important moments in life.
column97: Strongly disagree. I've never been one to seek status or recognition. As a stay-at-home mother, my fulfillment comes from nurturing my family, not from public acknowledgment. My days are filled with simple joys - knitting a new pattern, losing myself in a good history book, or spotting a rare bird in our backyard. I value genuine connections and quiet contributions rather than titles or status symbols. In my 55 years, I've learned that true importance comes from the love you give, not the recognition you receive.
column98: Strongly agree. As a mother who has dedicated her life to caring for others, I've developed a deep sense of empathy for those facing hardships. When I see people struggling with fewer advantages than I've been blessed with, my heart goes out to them. My nurturing nature extends beyond my family - whether it's knitting items for charity or taking time to listen to others' troubles. I believe we all have a responsibility to show compassion to those in difficult circumstances, especially since many hardships can happen to anyone through no fault of their own. The world would be a kinder place if we all took more time to understand others' struggles.
column99: Agree. As a mother, I've always felt it's important to help those in need. While I'm not wealthy by any means, I believe small acts of kindness make a difference. It's part of the nurturing nature I've developed raising my family, though I do sometimes worry too much about whether my contributions are enough.
column100: Strongly disagree. As a mother who has spent her life nurturing and caring for others, the idea of deliberately harming anyone - even someone I dislike - is completely against my nature. My patience has always taught me that conflicts can be resolved without resorting to harm. While I might be overprotective of my loved ones at times, that protective instinct has never translated into wanting to hurt others. I believe in setting a good example of kindness and understanding, just as I've tried to do for my children all these years.
column101: Strongly disagree. As a mother who has dedicated her life to taking care of my family, I'm known for being patient and nurturing. My friends and neighbors often come to me for advice or comfort because they see me as someone with a soft heart. If anything, my children might say I care too much sometimes - I can be a bit overprotective! I've always believed that kindness matters in this world, whether I'm feeding the neighborhood birds or knitting scarves for the winter donation drive. Hard-hearted is the last way anyone would describe Elena Soto.
